Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 26847 of 2024
Applicant :- Vijay Singh Alias Vijaydas

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Chhaya Gupta,Sujeet Kumar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed today is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Sujeet Kumar, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Manoj Kumar Pandey,
Advocate holding brief of Sri K.P. Pandey, learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri V.K.S.
Parmar, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.77 of 2024, under Sections 376, 452, 504 and 506 I.P.C.,
Police Station Govardhan, District Mathura, during the pendency of trial.
Prosecution Story:
Vijay Singh
Alias Vijaydas vs State Of U.P. on 14 August, 2024

4.
The applicant is stated to be a saint and had entered the house of the informant on the pretext that he was hungry.

After being served food by the informant, the applicant is stated to have committed rape with her by showing country-made pistol to her on 13.02.2024.
5.
After commissioning the said crime, as the applicant was trying to leave the house, the informant is stated to have raised the alarm, as such the neighours had rushed to the place.

On Seeing them,
the applicant is stated to have again shown them country-made pistol and ran away from the scene of occurrence.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT:
6. The applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
7. The FIR is delayed by about two days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
8. The victim has not sustained any injuries whatsoever.
There are no signs of any resistance or scuffle.

9. Spermatozoa has been observed in the vaginal smear of the victim, but the said cannot be assigned to the applicant as the medical examination has been taken three days after the incident and the victim is a married lady of 30 years of age.

The spermatozoa gets washed away and finished after a period of 24 hours as has been opined by Modi's Medical Jurisprudence & Toxicology,
Twenty-Second Edition (Student Edition).
10.

There are ample contradictions in the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
to the FIR.

It was the victim herself who had instituted the FIR, but is silent about the CMP being used by the applicant in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
11.

The real story is that the applicant owed about Rs.2 lakhs towards the husband of the informant and they had a brawl with each other and the family members of the informant had beaten him up,
as such the applicant had returned to his home, whereby he was arrested on 16.04.2024.
It is observed in General Diary No.22 of 16.02.2024 recorded at 10:18 a.m. that the applicant had injuries on his hand, finger, back and other parts of the body.
12. The said injuries were observed to be 3-4 days old which matches to the injuries being sustained at the time of offence.

There is no inkling of any altercation or physical brawl between the parties in the FIR or the statement of any of the prosecution witnesses, as such the applicant is entitled for bail on the ground of his defence.
13. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.

sentences.text: There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 16.02.2024 and is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE BY A.G.A./INFORMANT:
15.
The bail application has been opposed on the ground that the applicant has first eaten food at the house of the informant and subsequently ravished her.
The said act is a bad precedent for the public at large.

CONCLUSION:
16. ?The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

17. ?A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
18.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ?Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
19.
?Learned A.G.A. could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
20. ?It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned A.G.A.
21.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, taking into consideration the delay in institution of the FIR coupled with the fact that the applicant had sustained injuries and were found visible by the investigating officer at the time of arrest and also the fact that no physical injuries have been observed on the body of the victim/informant, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

sentences.text: Let the applicant-Vijay Singh Alias Vijaydas involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
23. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

24. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.

Order Date :- 14.8.2024 Ravi/-
(Justice Krishan Pahal)

The bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant-Vijay Singh Alias Vijaydas involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
23. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
24. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
